name: Slow Cooker Filipino Pork Adobo Bowls
intro_html: Filipino adobo is one of the great cheap dinners of the world, built on soy sauce, vinegar, and garlic. Lean pork loin slow cooks in that tangy sauce until tender, then goes over rice with green beans. At around ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) with {{protein}} grams of protein, this makes 14 bowls that punch way above their price.
ingredients_display: Bay Leaves (Great Value): 3 dried bay leaves (3 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Soy Sauce, 2/3 cup: ~$0.68. Buy 1 (covers about two batches).
Pantry seasonings (bay leaves, black pepper): ~$0.43. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $19.51 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.39 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $22.67 across 14 servings, roughly $1.62 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $4.66 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $27.33. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Adobo runs on pantry basics you likely already own. Lean on soy sauce and plain white vinegar, two of the cheapest flavor makers in the store.
Pork loin keeps this lean and affordable. Buy the loin over pre-cut pork and slice it yourself.
Frozen green beans mean no waste and no chopping. Keep a bag of frozen green beans ready for busy nights.
make_it: Add the pork loin, sliced onion, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns to the slow cooker.
Pour in the soy sauce and white vinegar and give it a stir.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork is tender.
Shred or chunk the pork and stir it back into the tangy sauce.
Steam the green beans until just tender and cook the rice.
Spoon the pork over rice and serve the green beans alongside.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings brings {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories.
